budget.cancellation: terminate then kill the active process tree, wait for reaping, and return a distinct timed-out or interrupted result

determinism.dependency_resolution: constraints.txt and explicitly pinned toolchain requirements define the reproducible set
determinism.output: UTF-8 with stable reason codes; elapsed timing and absolute paths are noncanonical diagnostics
determinism.platform_variation: unsupported optional backends or interpreters are explicit profile refusals, not silent skips
determinism.profile_order: the nine profile names and every command order are stable and manifest-defined
determinism.selection: pytest markers and exact paths define ownership; wall-clock duration and collection order never select a profile

effects.filesystem: bootstrap may create or modify only the selected environment and standard build, test, coverage, and documentation artifacts; checks are read-only except tool-owned caches
effects.network: bootstrap may contact configured package indexes; check and run operations require no network
effects.process: may execute Python, pip, build, ruff, pytest, coverage, mkdocs, twine, and documented smoke subprocesses with bounded timeouts and deterministic cleanup
effects.repository: never edits PLAN, TODO, PROGRESS, accepted contracts, frozen baseline evidence, or product source

ensures: Local and CI callers dispatch through the same repository-owned Python entry point and machine-readable profile manifest.
Every profile has an explicit purpose, dependency set, command set, supported platform and Python policy, and total and per-command timeout budget.
status remains dependency-free and validates only governance; runtime installs only the base package.
The status profile and its project-status-check command each have a finite 300-second budget so the append-only validator corpus can run without omitting or weakening any required check.
core excludes solver-only, discovery-owned, live-MCP, and slow selections and never imports python-sat.
solver owns tests marked requires_solver, installs the solvers extra, requires nauty where declared, and has a bounded fast-backend preflight.
discovery owns the dependency-minimal discovery and graph-budget selection without silently enabling solver or slow tests.
docs owns the pinned strict site build and executable documentation examples.
live-mcp owns the real subprocess-stdio contract tests and is supported only on the product Python 3.10 through 3.12 matrix.
slow owns explicitly marked expensive tests and never absorbs unmarked tests by filename or timing inference.
release owns pinned artifact tooling, wheel validation, clean installation, and installed-product smoke checks.
Coverage remains an explicit CI-owned command with the existing 85 percent floor; splitting profiles cannot delete, lower, skip, or relabel it green.
A missing, incompatible, skipped required command, timed-out, or failing command returns a distinct nonzero result and cannot make its profile green.
Human and JSON summaries identify the selected profile and every executed command without claiming excluded or unrun profiles.

epistemics.coverage_passed: the explicit coverage command completed and met the unchanged configured floor
epistemics.failed: at least one required command failed or a profile ownership invariant was violated
epistemics.not_run: the profile was described or excluded but not executed; never equivalent to passed
epistemics.passed: every required command in exactly the selected profile returned success
epistemics.timed_out: a required command exceeded its manifest budget and its process tree was reaped
epistemics.unsupported: the selected profile is incompatible with the declared platform, interpreter, or required executable policy

invariants: Profile names and meanings are stable within environment contract v3 and v1 and v2 remain immutable historical evidence.
The 300-second status budget changes time allowance only; it cannot remove, skip, relabel, or weaken any governance validator.
CI workflow commands call tools/dev.py rather than duplicating dependency, selection, or timeout semantics.
Every pytest test belongs to at least one declared execution profile and solver, live-MCP, and slow markers are fail-closed.
Core success never implies solver, discovery, docs, live-MCP, slow, coverage, or release success.
No profile reports green while one of its required commands is red, skipped, missing, timed out, or interrupted.
The coverage threshold remains 85 percent or higher and a coverage command is required by CI.
Supported CI matrix jobs use full Git history when validating the frozen legacy baseline.
The immutable MH-004 baseline artifact and observations remain byte-identical.
raises: No Python exception crosses the CLI boundary for an expected profile, dependency, capability, timeout, or subprocess failure.
An unknown profile or command, malformed manifest, overlap invariant violation, or missing required marker fails before product tests run.
Programmer defects may produce a traceback only in explicit debug mode.
requires: Python is one of the versions explicitly declared by the selected profile.
The command is executed from, or can discover, the repository root.
The selected profile is exactly one of status, runtime, core, solver, discovery, docs, live-mcp, slow, or release.
Network access is required only by bootstrap and clean-install operations.
Every CI job that replays the frozen legacy source fetches sufficient Git history to resolve its content-addressed source commit.
